claims.statement: The wiki lifecycle vocabulary is three status sets defined in the store and mirrored by the public WikiStatus enum: ACTIVE_STATUSES = {queued, fetching, generating, finalizing}, RUNNING_STATUSES = {fetching, generating, finalizing} and TERMINAL_STATUSES = {done, failed, cancelled}; these sets gate behavior (heartbeat only refreshes running rows, recover_stale sweeps only running rows, complete rejects non-terminal statuses, DELETE requires a terminal status) rather than being enforced by the database schema.

JobStore.claim_next is the only transition out of queued and is atomic: it opens BEGIN IMMEDIATE, selects the oldest queued row, then applies a conditional UPDATE ... WHERE status='queued' that sets status='fetching', claimed_by, a freshly minted claim_id, claimed_at and last_seen_at, resets cancel_requested=0, increments attempts by one, and sets started_at=COALESCE(started_at, ?) so the original start time survives every requeue; a rowcount other than 1 returns None when another worker won the race.

A wiki's internal lifecycle fields are exposed publicly as follows: claimed_by becomes worker, attempts is coerced to int, and status/progress/pages/size_bytes/error/created_at/started_at/finished_at are passed through, so a client can see which worker holds the attempt and how many times the wiki has been claimed.

JobStore.heartbeat is a single round-trip that refreshes the lease (last_seen_at) and optionally writes status, progress and pages; it first verifies that (wiki_id, claim_id) still exists and that the row is in RUNNING_STATUSES, returning {ok: False, cancel: True, status: <row status or None>} without writing otherwise, and on success returns the row's cancel_requested flag as cancel.

JobStore.complete writes a terminal state only when the caller still holds the live claim: it raises ValueError for a status outside TERMINAL_STATUSES, and its UPDATE is filtered by wiki_id AND claim_id AND status IN running statuses, so a reaped claim returns False and cannot overwrite a row another worker now owns; callers deliberately ignore that False.

Cancellation is asymmetric: JobStore.cancel writes status='cancelled' with finished_at and error='cancelled before start' immediately for a queued wiki, sets only cancel_requested=True (status untouched) for a running wiki and returns 'cancelling', and returns 'not_running' for terminal rows or 'not_found' for unknown ids, which POST /wikis/{id}/cancel translates into 200 'cancelled', 200 'cancelling', 409 and 404 respectively.

Delivery of a running cancellation flows only through the heartbeat: WorkerLoop._track sees result['cancel'] (or ok=False for a lost lease), sets the shared cancel_event and returns; the pipeline's check_cancel()/report() helpers raise PipelineCancelled, and run_openwiki watches the same event to kill the CLI subprocess, log '! openwiki killed: generation cancelled' and raise OpenWikiRunCancelled, which the pipeline re-raises as PipelineCancelled.

JobStore.recover_stale(lease_seconds) requeues every running row whose last_seen_at is NULL or older than the lease in one conditional UPDATE (status='queued', claim columns and last_seen_at cleared, cancel_requested=0) while preserving attempts; the API calls it once during create_app's lifespan startup and then every worker_reap_seconds from _reap_loop, so a crashed worker's claim is handed to another worker and, because the reaper clears cancel_requested, an orphaned claim is resumed rather than cancelled.

JobStore.retry accepts only failed/cancelled rows and requeues them by clearing the result and the whole claim (status='queued', error, progress, finished_at, cancel_requested, claimed_by, claim_id, claimed_at, last_seen_at) while leaving attempts and everything on disk untouched; POST /wikis/{id}/retry returns 202 queued, 409 not_retryable for any other status and 404 for unknown ids.

Resumption level 1 is the surviving workspace plus the reaper: pipeline._fetch first tests repo_dir/'.git' and, when it exists, logs 'repository workspace already present; resuming the generation' and returns without cloning or extracting, so a requeued claim handled by a different worker continues in the same <DATA_DIR>/jobs/<wiki_id>/repo directory; only a missing .git triggers a fresh fetch, and any leftover non-git directory is removed first.

Resumption level 2 is OpenWiki's own durable plan: wiki_runner.read_run_state parses openwiki/.run.json into {phase, total, completed, pending, current} by counting plan.pages[*].status == 'complete', returning None or a zeroed summary instead of raising for a missing, unparsable or oddly shaped file, and WorkerLoop._track reads it every worker_progress_seconds to feed the progress column (falling back to packer.count_pages for 'N pages written'), so a requeued CLI run picks up the unfinished pages of that plan instead of regenerating the wiki.

Run mode determines how much a resumed attempt costs: decide_mode resolves 'auto' against the workspace (update when openwiki/index.md exists, init otherwise, with an explicit update degrading to init when there are no docs), the resolved mode is written back with store.update(wiki_id, mode=mode), and in 'update' mode OpenWiki only rechecks the repository diff and stale claims, so a clean update performs no model work while 'init' regenerates the whole wiki and its Claims.

WorkerLoop._run is the single translator from outcomes to terminal states: a successful pipeline yields complete(status='done', pages, size_bytes, push_result); PipelineCancelled (user cancel or lost lease) yields cancelled; publisher.PushError yields failed with push_result.status='failed' while the packaged zip stays downloadable; ingestion.IngestionError, OpenWikiRunError (non-zero exit or JOB_TIMEOUT_MINUTES exceeded) and packer.PackError yield failed with the message; any other exception yields failed because a runner must never die; and asyncio.CancelledError is re-raised without writing anything, leaving the claim for the lease reaper.

A lost lease is terminal only for that attempt and is reported as cancelled rather than failed, which keeps the wiki eligible for retry: POST /wikis/{id}/retry re-enqueues it and the next worker resumes in the same workspace, so no cleanup on failure is what makes the retry path work.

Terminal rows are the only ones that can be removed: DELETE /wikis/{id} returns 409 while a wiki is still running and otherwise deletes the row together with the whole jobs/<wiki_id>/ directory (which also discards the resumability of that workspace), and purge_expired deletes terminal wikis whose finished_at is older than JOB_RETENTION_HOURS at startup, with 0 keeping everything forever.

Artifact readiness is a separate signal from status: GET /wikis/{id}/download answers 404 'wiki is not ready (status=...)' whenever wiki.zip does not exist (e.g. while running or after a failure before packaging), whereas a retried wiki whose previous attempt already packaged a zip keeps serving that older archive until packer.pack_wiki atomically replaces the destination through a .tmp file.

The lifecycle is observable through GET /wikis/{id} (status, worker = claimed_by, attempts, progress, pages, size_bytes, error, push_result, started_at, finished_at), GET /wikis/{id}/logs?tail=N over the worker-written log, and GET /health, which publishes pool = store.stats() counting queued rows, running rows and workers seen within worker_ttl_seconds (120 s by default); worker identity recorded as claimed_by is WORKER_ID when set, otherwise the container hostname.

Lifecycle timing is configured entirely through Settings: worker_lease_seconds (180) is the age of last_seen_at at which recover_stale requeues a running row, worker_reap_seconds (30) is the API sweep interval, worker_progress_seconds (2.0) is the heartbeat/progress period and therefore the effective lease refresh rate, worker_poll_seconds (2.0) is the idle claim retry delay, max_concurrent_jobs (1) is the generations per container (scaled with replicas), job_timeout_minutes (45) bounds the CLI subprocess, and job_retention_hours (0) controls purging of terminal wikis.

The `wikis` row in `<DATA_DIR>/openwiki.db` written by `app/core/storage.py` is the single lifecycle truth for a generation: the API creates the row, a worker claims it, progress is reported into it through heartbeats, and only the holder of the live claim writes its terminal state; logs, the workspace under `jobs/<wiki_id>/` and `wiki.zip` are side artifacts rather than lifecycle owners.

Each lifecycle status has exactly one writer: `JobStore.create`, `JobStore.retry` and `JobStore.recover_stale` write `queued`; `JobStore.claim_next` writes `fetching`; the pipeline's `report(status=...)` writes `generating` (before the CLI run) and `finalizing` (after it, before packaging); and `JobStore.complete` writes the terminal `done`/`failed`/`cancelled` together with `finished_at`, which is also set by the immediate cancel of a queued row.

Errors persisted on a row are truncated to 500 characters before being stored, bounding the growth of the `error` column; the push-failure path applies the same truncation to the message stored in `error` and to the `detail` recorded in `push_result` with `status: failed`.

Because `openwiki/.run.json` is transient resume state rather than a wiki artifact, `publisher.publish_wiki` stages the artifact directory with an explicit exclusion pathspec (`:(exclude)<artifact_dir>/.run.json`), so the push-back commit never carries the file that makes a requeued generation resume.
